items.stem: Most of a product's lifecycle cost is typically:

options.rationale: Correct: design decisions lock in the majority of eventual cost.
Production reveals cost, but design commits it.
Marketing does not commit manufacturing cost.

options.text: Equal to the raw-material price alone
options.rationale: Material is only part of the committed cost.

items.explanation: Correct: design decisions lock in the majority of eventual cost.

items.stem: Which TWO are core DFA strategies? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Reduce the total number of parts
options.rationale: Correct: fewer parts cut assembly time and cost.

options.text: Design parts so they can only be assembled the correct way

options.rationale: Extra fasteners increase assembly cost and time.

options.text: Require special tools for every joint
options.rationale: Special tools raise assembly difficulty and cost.

items.explanation: Correct: fewer parts cut assembly time and cost.

items.stem: Specifying tighter tolerances than necessary tends to:

options.text: Increase manufacturing cost without improving function
options.rationale: Correct: unnecessary tight tolerances raise cost for no functional gain.
Tighter tolerances generally cost more, not less.

options.text: Have no effect on cost at all
options.rationale: Tolerances have a strong effect on process cost.

options.text: Guarantee the part will never fail
options.rationale: Tolerance alone does not guarantee against all failure.

items.explanation: Correct: unnecessary tight tolerances raise cost for no functional gain.
